frontMatter.introduction: This SOP Manual has been developed to provide a structured framework for managing the environmental, social, and operational practices of Sri All India Exports. It ensures that all employees, contractors, and stakeholders follow standardized procedures that align with local regulations, international standards, and the company’s sustainability commitments.
frontMatter.objective:
The purpose of this manual is to:
Provide a single reference guide for all operational and sustainability-related SOPs.
Ensure consistency and compliance in day-to-day operations across all departments and sites.
Reduce environmental, social, and safety risks by standardizing best practices.
Support transparency and accountability during internal reviews, audits, and customer assessments.

Objectives
Promote continuous improvement in sustainability, safety, and compliance.
Ensure responsible resource use, waste management, and pollution prevention.
Enhance worker safety and wellbeing through proper training and operational controls.
Strengthen customer and stakeholder confidence by demonstrating ethical and sustainable practices.
frontMatter.scope:
This SOP Manual applies to:
All Sri All India Exports facilities, including production, dyeing, washing, packaging, logistics, and administration.
All employees, contractors, suppliers, and third-party service providers engaged in operations.
All SOPs listed in this manual, including those related to energy, water, hazardous waste, product sustainability, worker safety, and compliance.
frontMatter.reviewMechanism:
This SOP will be reviewed every two years by the Environmental & Sustainability Office to assess its effectiveness in reducing water consumption, optimizing recycling systems, and ensuring wastewater compliance. The review will include evaluation of risk assessments, dyeing and washing efficiency, and rainwater harvesting performance. Updates will be made to integrate new technologies and meet future sustainability goals.

Review Frequency: SOPs must be reviewed every two years or earlier if significant operational or regulatory changes occur.
Approval Authority: All SOPs must be approved by the Environmental Manager and the Managing Director before implementation.

sops.title: Workplace Safety Incident & Risk Management System

blocks.text: This SOP outlines the procedures for identifying, reporting, and managing workplace safety incidents, risks, and concerns at Sri All India Exports. The aim is to ensure a safe working environment for all employees by minimizing hazards and promoting a culture of safety awareness.

This SOP applies to all employees, contractors, and visitors at Sri All India Exports across all locations. It covers procedures for reporting and addressing safety incidents, conducting risk assessments, and implementing corrective actions.

narrative.text:
Immediate Reporting: Employees must report any workplace safety incident or near-miss to their supervisor immediately. Examples include slips, trips, falls, equipment malfunctions, and exposure to hazardous materials.
Use the designated reporting channels:
Email: ramesh@sriallindia.com
Contact Person: P.Ramesh
Incident Documentation: The supervisor will document the incident using the Workplace Safety Incident Report Form, including details such as the date, time, location, persons involved, and a brief description of the incident.
Initial Response: The supervisor will take immediate steps to secure the area and prevent further incidents. This may include cordoning off the area, providing first aid, or shutting down equipment.

blocks.text:
Conducting Risk Assessments: Annual risk assessments must be conducted in all work areas to identify potential hazards. This includes evaluating the safety of machinery, tools, materials, and working conditions.
Risk Register: All identified risks must be recorded in a Risk Register, with details on the nature of the risk, the likelihood of occurrence, potential impact, and control measures in place.
Implementation of Control Measures: Appropriate control measures must be implemented to mitigate identified risks. This can include engineering controls, administrative controls, and personal protective equipment (PPE).

body.text: A team comprising members of the Safety Committee and relevant supervisors will investigate all reported incidents.
The investigation team will conduct a root cause analysis to identify underlying causes and contributing factors to the incident.
Based on the findings, the team will recommend CAPAs to prevent recurrence. The implementation of these actions will be tracked and documented.

blocks.text: Mandatory Safety Training: All employees must undergo safety training during onboarding and receive regular refresher courses. Topics covered will include hazard identification, safe work practices, and emergency response procedures.

responsibilities: Report any safety incidents or concerns immediately to the supervisor or Safety Officer.
Follow all safety procedures and participate in safety training.
Ensure safety procedures are followed and report incidents to the Safety Officer.
Conduct regular safety inspections and address any safety concerns.
Assess and respond to reported incidents.
Conduct risk assessments and implement safety measures.
Maintain incident and training records.
Review and approve safety procedures and protocols.
Provide resources and support for safety initiatives.

blocks.text: This SOP will be reviewed by the Health and Safety Manager Every Two year or following any significant incident to ensure its continued relevance and effectiveness in maintaining workplace safety standards.

This SOP outlines the measures and technologies implemented by Sri All India Exports to prevent and mitigate air pollution from its cotton fabric manufacturing processes. The SOP aims to ensure compliance with environmental regulations, enhance sustainability practices, and protect the health and safety of employees and the surrounding community.

This SOP applies to all operations at Sri All India Exports, including handloom and power loom manufacturing. It is applicable to all employees, contractors, and personnel involved in production, maintenance, and management activities.

substeps.text: Routine Monitoring: Conduct annual ambient air monitoring for PM10, PM2.5, SO2, and NOx to assess the environmental impact.
Equipment Maintenance: Schedule regular inspections and preventive maintenance for all critical equipment to prevent leaks and malfunctions.
Employee Training: Provide comprehensive training programs on environmental policies, spill prevention, and emergency response.
Enclosures: Enclose dust-generating processes like weaving and cutting to contain particulate emissions.
Housekeeping: Maintain clean work areas using industrial vacuum systems to minimize dust accumulation.
Activated Carbon Filters: Install activated carbon filters in exhaust systems to capture and neutralize VOCs.
Low-VOC Materials: Use low-VOC dyes, adhesives, and solvents in manufacturing processes.
Closed-Loop System: The plant is designed with an enclosure system to ensure a closed-loop process for sulfur absorption, particularly in viscose manufacturing.
Monitoring and Maintenance: Regularly monitor the performance of the sulfur recovery system, ensuring optimal operation and minimal emissions.
Sound Barriers: Install sound barriers around high-decibel equipment to reduce noise pollution.
Operational Scheduling: Schedule noisy operations during daytime hours to minimize disturbance.
Noise Monitoring: Conduct Annual noise monitoring in high-noise areas.
Activated Carbon Filters: Use these filters in exhaust systems to neutralize odorous compounds.
Material Handling: Store odorous materials in sealed containers and handle them in well-ventilated areas.
Optimized Delivery Scheduling: Schedule deliveries and dispatches during off-peak hours to reduce traffic congestion.
Route Planning: Implement efficient route planning for company vehicles to avoid congested areas and reduce transit times.
Vehicle Maintenance: Ensure all company vehicles are regularly maintained for optimal fuel efficiency and minimal emissions during transit.

narrative.text:
Annually Assessments: Conduct Annually assessments to track progress in emission control.
Data Analysis: Analyze data on emission levels and maintenance activities to ensure compliance.
Internal Audits: Conduct annual internal audits to review the effectiveness of the air pollution management system, identifying areas for improvement and ensuring that all procedures are being followed.
Reporting: The Environmental Manager prepares reports summarizing findings and submits them to senior management.

Incident Documentation: Document all incidents involving pollutant releases, including causes, response actions, and outcomes.
Response Evaluation: Conduct evaluations following each incident to identify root causes and implement corrective actions.
Corrective Action Plan: Develop and implement corrective action plans based on incident evaluations to prevent future occurrences.
Regulatory Reporting: Ensure all necessary reports are filed with local and national environmental agencies in accordance with legal requirements.

sops.title: Sustainable Product Recovery and Disposal Strategy

blocks.text: This SOP outlines the protocols and procedures implemented by Sri All India Exports to enhance product sustainability through efficient use and storage practices, resource-efficient product design, and innovations to minimize microfiber shedding. The aim is to extend product life, reduce environmental impacts during product use, and ensure compliance with international sustainability standards.

This SOP applies to all Sri All India Exports operations related to product design, development, manufacturing, and customer information sharing. It is applicable to employees, contractors, suppliers, and customers who are involved in the lifecycle of products, from production to end use.

steps.heading: Efficient Use, Storage, and Maintenance to Extend Product Life

substeps.text: Provide customers with clear instructions on best practices for using and maintaining textile products to extend their useful life.
For chemical-based products, ensure users are informed of correct storage conditions to prevent leaks or emissions.
Publish guidance on resource-efficient washing practices (e.g., low-temperature wash, minimal detergent use).
Conduct awareness programs for employees and distributors on correct product handling and safe storage.

steps.heading: Design for Reduced Resource Input in Product Use

substeps.text: Develop and introduce designs that minimize resource consumption during use, such as energy-efficient equipment, water-saving nozzles, and optimized fabrics requiring fewer consumables.
Conduct R&D to identify design modifications that reduce water, electricity, and chemical usage.
Integrate eco-design principles into all new product development cycles.
Regularly benchmark against industry best practices for resource-efficient product designs.

steps.heading: Design or Treatment to Minimize Microfiber Shedding and Tearing

substeps.text: Introduce treatments for yarns and fabrics to strengthen fibers, reducing microfiber release during washing.
Adopt compact weaving/knitting techniques to enhance durability and minimize tearing.
Collaborate with research labs and chemical suppliers to identify eco-friendly coating or finishing methods that reduce microfiber loss.
Conduct product testing in washing simulations to measure and control microfiber shedding before market release.

Ensures compliance with eco-design and sustainability standards.
Prepares and submits sustainability reports to management and regulators.
Integrates eco-design principles into product development.

Monitors implementation of sustainable materials and designs.
Conducts product testing for durability and microfiber shedding.
Ensures products meet safety and sustainability criteria before release.

Findings will be used to update product design guidelines, improve maintenance information, and align with evolving sustainability standards.

sops.title: IT Security Incident Handling & Recovery Procedure
sops.owner: IT Security Manager and Data Protection Officer

blocks.text: This SOP outlines the procedures for detecting, responding to, and managing security incidents to prevent further damage and protect sensitive information. It aims to ensure a swift and effective response to security incidents and to improve overall information security.
This procedure applies to all employees, contractors, and third parties with access to the company's information systems and data across all locations.

rows.definition: An event that compromises the confidentiality, integrity, or availability of information or information systems.
A designated team responsible for managing and responding to security incidents.

blocks.text:
Detect and respond to information security incidents promptly.
Limit the impact of security breaches.
Prevent further damage and reassure affected parties.
Document and learn from incidents to enhance security measures.

body.text: Initial Detection: All employees must report any suspicious activity or potential security breaches immediately (within 1 hour of discovery) to the IT Security Team. Indicators of a breach include unusual system behavior, unauthorized access attempts, or unexpected data anomalies. All reports must include an initial assessment of the threat level, indicating whether it is high, medium, or low.

Reporting: Report the incident to the IT Security Team using the designated channels: Name: P.Ramesh Phone: +91 9843031484. Provide the following information: Time and date of the incident; Description of the incident; Systems or data affected; Initial actions taken; Threat level assessment (high, medium, low).

Initial Alert: The IT Security Team will evaluate the report and confirm if a security breach has occurred. If confirmed, notify the Data Protection Team, Sri All India Exports Directors, and other key stakeholders within 2 hours of detection. Determine if external cybersecurity experts need to be involved and engage them if necessary.

Containment: Implement immediate actions to contain the breach and prevent further damage. This includes isolating affected systems, revoking access rights, or shutting down services. Document all containment actions taken. Verify that all containment actions are successful and that no further unauthorized access or data loss is occurring.

Breach Assessment: The Data Protection Team, in collaboration with the IT Security Team, will perform a thorough assessment of the breach within 24 hours of containment. Evaluate the scope, cause, and impact of the breach, including the number of affected individuals and any potential data compromise. Identify and document the vulnerabilities exploited during the breach.

Risk Evaluation: Assess potential harm to the company, data subjects, and partners. Determine if the breach meets the criteria for mandatory reporting to authorities. Seek approval from Sri All India Exports Directors for further actions. Assess the financial and reputational impact of the breach.

Decision to Notify: Based on the assessment, decide if notification to authorities and/or individuals is required. Seek approval from Sri All India Exports Directors and consult with legal advisors if necessary. Ensure that notifications are made within regulatory timelines and include all required information.

Notification Process: Notify affected parties, including data controllers, data subjects, and relevant authorities as required. Provide clear and concise information about the breach, potential risks, and steps being taken to mitigate the impact. Ensure that all communications are consistent, transparent, and offer guidance on protective actions for affected parties.

CAPAs Implementation: Implement Corrective and Preventive Actions (CAPAs) to address the root cause of the breach and prevent recurrence. Verify and document the implementation of CAPAs. Develop and maintain a detailed incident report that includes findings, actions taken, and lessons learned.

Containment History Log: Maintain a detailed log of the containment and mitigation actions taken during the incident response. Include timestamps, responsible personnel, and outcomes for each action in the log.

Review and Learn: Conduct a post-incident review to identify lessons learned and opportunities for improvement. Update the Incident Response Procedure and related policies based on the review findings. Incorporate feedback from all stakeholders involved in the response process to enhance future incident handling.

responsibilities: Detect, report, and respond to security incidents.
Implement containment and mitigation actions.
Collaborate with the Data Protection Team for breach assessment and risk evaluation.
Lead the breach assessment and risk evaluation process.
Coordinate notification efforts and communication with regulatory bodies.
Ensure compliance with relevant regulations.
Report any suspicious activity or potential security breaches immediately.
Follow instructions from the IT Security Team and Data Protection Team during incident response.

sops.title: Authorization & Approval Process for Critical Transactions

blocks.text: This SOP outlines the procedure for the approval of sensitive transactions, including gifts and travel expenses, to ensure compliance with company policies, ethical standards, and regulatory requirements. The goal is to prevent conflicts of interest, ensure transparency, and uphold the integrity of the company.
This procedure applies to all employees, contractors, and third parties who are involved in or responsible for initiating, approving, or processing sensitive transactions at Sri All India Exports.

rows.definition: Transactions involving gifts, travel, or other benefits that may create a conflict of interest or influence business decisions.
Designated individuals or departments responsible for reviewing and approving sensitive transactions.

body.text: All sensitive transactions must be identified and documented. Examples include gifts exceeding a specified monetary threshold, business travel for non-routine purposes, or other benefits.
Thresholds: Gifts or benefits valued above ₹5,000 and travel expenses above ₹25,000 require specific approval.

Complete a Sensitive Transaction Request Form for each transaction. This form should include: Name of the recipient; Description of the transaction (gift, travel, etc.); Monetary value; Purpose of the transaction; Date and location; Justification for the transaction and any supporting documentation (e.g., travel itineraries, invoices).

Submit the completed Sensitive Transaction Request Form to the immediate supervisor or department head for an initial review. The supervisor will evaluate the transaction for compliance with company policies and potential conflicts of interest.

Transactions requiring approval should be submitted to the following authorities based on the value. Gifts: Above ₹5,000: Department Head; Above ₹10,000: Senior Management. Travel Expenses: Above ₹25,000: Senior Management; Above ₹50,000: Executive Committee.

The approving authority will review the documentation and justification provided. They may request additional information if needed. Approval or rejection of the transaction must be documented in writing, including reasons for approval or denial.

Processing: Once approved, process the transaction according to company procedures. Ensure that all documentation is complete and accurate. For travel expenses, ensure that travel arrangements are booked in accordance with company travel policies.

Recording: Maintain a record of all sensitive transactions, including approvals, supporting documentation, and any related correspondence. Records should be retained for a minimum of 5 years and made available for audit or review as needed.

Post-Transaction Review: Conduct annual reviews of sensitive transactions to ensure compliance with policies and identify any potential issues or patterns. Review findings should be documented and reported to the relevant authorities for further action if required.

sops.title: Data Access Control & Customer Data Management Framework

blocks.text: This SOP outlines the internal controls and procedures implemented by Sri All India Exports to restrict unauthorized access to customer or client data, both physical and digital. It also provides guidelines on consulting and informing customers about the collection, storage, and sharing of their personal data.

This SOP applies to all employees, contractors, and third parties who have access to customer or client data within Sri All India Exports. It encompasses data handling processes across all departments and locations.

rows.definition: Personal and sensitive information collected from customers or clients, including names, addresses, contact details, payment information, and any other data shared during transactions.
Access to data by individuals or entities not explicitly granted permission to view, modify, or use the data.
A timetable that specifies the duration for which different categories of data are kept and the actions to be taken at the end of the retention period.

substeps.text: Restricted Areas: Customer data is stored in secured areas accessible only to authorized personnel. Access to these areas requires security clearance and is monitored by CCTV. For example, physical copies of purchase orders and invoices containing customer addresses and payment details are kept in locked cabinets within a secured room.

Document Handling: Physical documents containing customer data must be stored in locked cabinets or rooms with restricted access. Employees must sign in and out when accessing these documents. Sensitive documents like contracts, legal agreements, and customer identification proofs are strictly controlled and logged.

User Authentication: All employees accessing digital data systems must use unique user IDs and strong passwords. Multi-factor authentication (MFA) is enforced for sensitive data access. For instance, employees must enter a password and a one-time code sent to their mobile device to access the customer database.

Access Permissions: Data access permissions are granted based on job roles and responsibilities. Employees only have access to the data necessary for their tasks. Regular audits are conducted to ensure compliance. For example, only the finance team can access customer payment details, while the sales team can view contact information and order history.

Data Encryption: Sensitive customer data is encrypted both in transit and at rest. Encryption keys are securely stored and managed. Emails containing customer details are encrypted before sending, and databases storing personal information are protected with strong encryption algorithms.

Third-Party Access: Access to customer data by third-party vendors or service providers is restricted and granted only when necessary. Contracts include clauses ensuring data protection compliance. For example, a third-party logistics provider is given access only to customer shipping addresses for order fulfilment.

Activity Logs: All access to customer data is logged, including the date, time, and user involved. Logs are regularly reviewed for any unauthorized access attempts. If a breach attempt is detected, an alert is immediately sent to the IT security team.

Regular Audits: Data access controls are subject to regular internal audits to identify vulnerabilities and ensure adherence to this SOP. Audits include reviewing access logs, verifying encryption standards, and assessing third-party compliance.

Transparency: Customers are informed about the types of data being collected, the purpose of collection, and how it will be used at the time of data collection. For example, customers are notified that their contact information is collected for order processing and delivery notifications.

Consent: Explicit consent is obtained from customers before collecting their personal data, especially for sensitive information. Customers have the right to opt out of data collection where applicable. For instance, consent is required to collect and store customer bank account details for payment processing
Data Retention: Customers are informed about the duration for which their data will be stored and the criteria used to determine this period.

Third-Party Sharing: If customer data is shared with third parties (e.g., for shipping or payment processing), customers are informed of the entities involved and the purpose of sharing. Third-party partners are vetted to ensure they comply with data protection standards. For example, shipping addresses are shared with logistics providers solely for the purpose of order delivery.

Access Requests: Customers have the right to request access to their data, request corrections, or ask for their data to be deleted. These requests are handled promptly and in accordance with data protection laws. For instance, a customer can request the deletion of their account and all associated personal information if they decide to stop using the company's services.

Communication Channels: Customers can contact the company via email: ramesh@sriallindia.com or Tel: +91 4324 237140 Or Fax: +91 4324 231484 for any queries regarding their personal data. A designated Person is available to address these concerns. Contact information for the Person is provided Below: Name: P.Ramesh Phone: +91 9843031484.

Immediate Notification: In the event of a data breach that compromises customer data, affected customers are notified promptly. The notification includes details of the breach, the data affected, and the steps being taken to mitigate the impact. For example, if unauthorized access to customer email addresses is detected, the company will notify all affected customers and advise them on how to secure their accounts.
Follow-up Support: The company provides support to customers following a breach, including offering credit monitoring services or guidance on securing their personal information.

sops.title: Hazardous Waste Management and Disposal Procedure

blocks.text: This SOP outlines the protocols and procedures implemented by Sri All India Exports for the safe labelling, storage, handling, and transportation of hazardous substances. The aim is to minimize environmental impact and exposure, ensure compliance with environmental regulations, and safeguard the health and safety of employees and the surrounding community.

This SOP applies to all operations at Sri All India Exports, including the management of hazardous substances used in handloom and power loom manufacturing processes. It is applicable to all employees, contractors, and personnel involved in production, maintenance, and management activities related to hazardous materials.

substeps.text: Standardized labelling: Ensure all hazardous substances are labelled according to the Globally Harmonized System (GHS) standards, including hazard symbols, risk phrases, and safety precautions. Labels must be reviewed and updated every 6 months.
Language and Clarity: Labels must be in the local language and English, ensuring clarity and accessibility for all employees.
Regular Inspections: Conduct monthly inspections to verify that labels remain intact, legible, and accurate.

Dedicated Storage Areas: Store hazardous substances in designated, well-ventilated areas away from incompatible materials, with clear signage indicating restricted access. Conduct an assessment every 3 months to ensure compliance.
Secondary Containment: Utilize secondary containment systems (e.g., spill pallets, bunds) to prevent leaks and spills from contaminating the environment.
Environmental Controls: Implement temperature and humidity controls in storage areas to maintain safe conditions for hazardous substances. Monitor these conditions daily.
Inventory Management: Maintain a detailed inventory of all hazardous substances, regularly updated to ensure accurate records. Inventory checks should be performed every 30 days.

Personal Protective Equipment (PPE): Provide appropriate PPE (e.g., gloves, goggles, respirators) to all personnel handling hazardous substances and enforce its use. PPE must be inspected weekly for wear and tear.
Training Programs: Conduct annualy training on safe handling procedures, including emergency response protocols in case of spills or exposure.
Controlled Handling Areas: Restrict handling activities to controlled areas with proper ventilation and spill containment measures.
Certified Transport Vehicles: Use vehicles certified for hazardous materials transportation, equipped with spill response kits and proper signage. Vehicles should be inspected every 15 days.
Driver Training: Ensure drivers are trained in the safe transport of hazardous substances, including emergency response in case of accidents. Training refreshers should be held every 6 months.
Documentation: Accompany all hazardous materials with proper documentation, including Material Safety Data Sheets (MSDS), transport manifests, and emergency contact information.
Route Planning: Plan transportation routes to avoid populated areas and environmentally sensitive zones, minimizing risk during transit. Routes should be reviewed and optimized every 3 months.

steps.heading: Specialized Treatment and Safe Disposal of Hazardous Substances

substeps.text: Waste Segregation: Separate hazardous waste from non-hazardous waste at the source, ensuring proper labelling and containment. Segregation procedures should be reviewed every 2 months.
Neutralization and Treatment: Implement neutralization or chemical treatment processes before disposal to reduce toxicity and environmental impact.
Waste Minimization: Implement strategies to minimize hazardous waste generation through process optimization and material substitution.
Documentation and Reporting: Maintain detailed records of hazardous waste disposal, including quantities, disposal methods, and certificates of destruction. Reports should be compiled monthly.

steps.heading: Recovery and Reuse of Input Materials

substeps.text: Recovery Practices: Adopt processes to recover and reuse scrap materials such as paper, wood, fabrics, and packaging materials within operations.
Repurposing: Repurpose old or used equipment for alternative functions to extend useful life and reduce waste.
Monitoring: Maintain monthly records of recovered and reused input materials and track reductions in raw material consumption.

steps.heading: Substitution with Safer and Less Hazardous Materials

substeps.text: Substitution Practices: Replace highly toxic chemicals with safer alternatives such as non-chlorinated bleaching agents, organic or vegetable-based inks, and eco-friendly solvents.
Continuous Review: Periodically evaluate chemical inventories to identify hazardous substances that can be replaced with less harmful alternatives.
Compliance: Ensure all alternative materials meet industry standards and reduce risks to workers, consumers, and the environment.
Documentation: Maintain records of substituted materials and report improvements annually.

This SOP outlines the protocols and procedures adopted by Sri All India Exports to reduce environmental impact by improving energy efficiency, installing waste heat recovery systems, reducing carbon emissions in transportation, and implementing employee training and sustainable packaging initiatives. The objective is to ensure continuous improvement in sustainability performance, align with international environmental standards, and strengthen our long-term commitment to a green supply chain.

This SOP applies to all company operations, including production, dyeing, logistics, packaging, and administrative facilities of Sri All India Exports. It covers employees, contractors, and service providers directly or indirectly involved in activities impacting energy, emissions, and sustainability.

steps.heading: Energy Efficiency through Technology & Equipment Upgrades

substeps.text: Assessment & Selection: Conduct annual energy audits to identify high-consumption machinery and processes. Select new equipment/technology with at least 20–30% higher efficiency compared to industry benchmarks.
Implementation Protocols: Replace conventional looms, boilers, pumps, motors, and lighting with energy-efficient alternatives. Install smart energy meters to monitor energy usage in real time.
Verification: Compare pre- and post-upgrade energy consumption data. Conduct quarterly reviews to verify sustained energy savings.

steps.heading: Implementation of Waste Heat Recovery and Cogeneration Systems

substeps.text: System Design : Install heat exchangers in dyeing and boiler units to capture energy from hot wastewater or exhaust steam. Assess and implement CHP or cogeneration systems for simultaneous heat and power generation.
Operational Protocols: Maintain daily logs of recovered heat and power generation. Conduct weekly preventive maintenance of heat exchangers and CHP equipment.
Monitoring: Track daily recovered steam/hot water in operational records. Publish an annual report quantifying total energy and CO₂ savings.

steps.heading: Reduction of Greenhouse Gas Emissions in Transportation

substeps.text: Fleet Management: Replace older vehicles with fuel-efficient, electric, or biofuel-powered vehicles. Install GPS-enabled route optimization systems to minimize distance and reduce empty miles.
Operational Protocols: Track fuel consumption and CO₂ emissions on a monthly basis. Promote carpooling and shared transport for employees to reduce commuting emissions.
Verification: Compare fuel and emission data before and after interventions.

Training Modules: Provide annual training on energy conservation, sustainable production, and workplace eco-practices. Conduct specialized training for machine operators on efficient machine handling.
Frequency: Induction training for all new employees.

narrative.text:
Routine Inspections: Conduct quarterly inspections of energy-efficient equipment, waste heat systems, and transport operations to ensure compliance with sustainability protocols.
Data Analysis: Analyze energy usage, CO₂ emissions, and packaging reports monthly to identify areas for improvement. Data should be reviewed annually for trend analysis.

Incident Documentation: Document all incidents (e.g., equipment malfunction, energy inefficiency, transport emission deviation) within 24 hours.
Response Evaluation: Evaluate corrective actions within 7 days to identify root causes and prevent recurrence.

This SOP outlines the protocols and procedures adopted by Sri All India Exports to optimize water usage, recycle and reuse wastewater, adopt water-saving dyeing methods, minimize water consumption in washing processes, and strengthen water risk assessment and monitoring. Additionally, it establishes guidelines for rainwater harvesting and groundwater recharge to further enhance sustainable water management. The objective is to reduce freshwater dependency, ensure responsible wastewater discharge, and align with global sustainability standards.

This SOP applies to all company operations, including dyeing, washing, cleaning, utility, and support processes at Sri All India Exports. It is applicable to all employees, contractors, and third-party service providers involved in production, utilities, and environmental monitoring.

steps.heading: Technologies or Practices to Recycle or Reuse Water

substeps.text: Install effluent treatment plants (ETP) and water recycling units to reclaim water from production and washing processes.
Reuse treated water for non-potable purposes such as cooling, irrigation, and process cleaning.
Implement closed-loop systems for dye baths and finishing units to minimize freshwater intake.
Monitor water recovery ratio monthly to ensure efficiency above 70%.

steps.heading: Adoption of Waterless or Water-Saving Dyeing Methods

substeps.text: Introduce low-water dyeing machines and technologies such as air dye or foam dyeing methods.
Adopt low-water dyeing agents and nozzles to reduce water consumption per batch.
Regularly review and optimize dye recipes to align with water-saving practices.
Conduct trials of innovative technologies for potential adoption across processes.

steps.heading: Reduction of Water Consumption in Washing and Cleaning Processes

substeps.text: Install water-efficient washing machines with flow control systems.
Adopt counter-current washing techniques to reduce water use per cycle.
Recycle wastewater from washing units after treatment for reuse in preliminary washing.
Regularly calibrate and maintain washing machinery to avoid unnecessary water losses.
Conduct annual risk assessments to identify water scarcity, discharge risks, and compliance gaps.
Monitor wastewater parameters (COD, BOD, TSS, pH) in line with Pollution Control Board norms.
Submit quarterly wastewater compliance reports to local authorities.
Install online monitoring systems for real-time tracking of wastewater discharge quality.
Implement rooftop rainwater collection systems to reduce freshwater dependency.
Install recharge pits to replenish groundwater levels in surrounding areas.
Maintain annual records of rainwater collected, stored, and reused.
Integrate rainwater usage into non-critical operations such as gardening, cooling, and floor cleaning.
